summary: Each letter was shifted forward by key + its position, so we shift it back by the same amount, wrapping around the alphabet with `% 26` (T4 — character shifting). Case is kept and non-letters stay as they are.

blocks.title: Read the text and the key
blocks.text: The text stays a string; the key is converted to `int` because we do math with it.

blocks.title: Collect the decoded characters
blocks.text: We append characters to a list and join it once at the end — clean and fast.

blocks.title: Work out the shift for this position
blocks.text: `enumerate` gives the 0-based index `i` with each character. The shift grows by one per position: `key + i`. The index counts every character, including spaces and symbols.

blocks.title: Shift a lowercase letter back
blocks.text: `ord(ch) - ord('a')` turns `a..z` into 0..25. We subtract the shift, wrap with `% 26`, and add `ord('a')` back. In Python `%` never gives a negative result, so `(3 - 5) % 26` is 24 — no `+ 26` needed like in C.

blocks.title: Shift an uppercase letter back
blocks.text: Same formula with `'A'` as the base, so uppercase stays uppercase.

blocks.title: Leave other characters alone
blocks.text: Digits, spaces and symbols are copied unchanged.

blocks.title: Join and print
blocks.text: `''.join(out)` glues the list into one string: `Decoded string: hello`.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 1000 characters — instant.
pitfalls: Losing the case by always using `'a'` as the base.
